- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward quickly — overcorrects or lags in mean reversion.
- Forecast mean is consistently higher than true mean — model exhibits upward bias.
- Model underreacts to recent downward trends; fails to adjust forecast downward when prices show clear downward momentum.
- Forecast variance is too high — model overreacts to short-term noise, especially in the middle of the horizon.
- Model often fails to capture the “reversion to mean” behavior after strong upward moves — tends to hold high values longer than observed.
- Forecast for day 1 is often too high — may be overfitting to recent high values or ignoring macroeconomic signals.
- Model underestimates the impact of policy changes or supply shocks — tends to ignore structural shifts in the short term.
- Forecast for last 3–5 days often shows downward drift but not enough — model undercorrects for near-term mean reversion.
- Model exhibits “lagged response” — reacts to price changes with a delay, especially after spikes or drops.
